title: EGY-16 · Writing in Egyptian: messages, greetings and condolences

blocks.text: EGY-16 · Writing in Egyptian: messages, greetings and
condolences
Lesson overview

While ARZ units teach you to read the written dialect, this unity teaches you to write it: a message to a friend, an invitation, a voice message, and above all formulas for occasions (birthdays, marriages, births, outdated examinations, diseases, mourning, religious holidays), which in Egypt are almost mandatory and always have a fixed response. Wronging a formula is not serious, but knowing them well is a sign of respect that Egyptians notice and appreciate. You will also learn to choose the log (Egyptian or fuṣḥā simple) according to the recipient. Nine weeks, in parallel with B2-12INT-04INT-05, the Test B2.2 and the beginning of B2-13.

rows: 12–13 9 weeks (weeks) 202–210), about 1,5 hours per week in two blocks

blocks.text: Materials This unit, a tutor or an Egyptian partner, an Arabic keyboard on your phone or computer
Targets. At the end of the unit you know:
1. write in Arabic characters a clear and consistent Egyptian message in the graphs;
2. use formulas for happy occasions and their answers;
3. tactfully write a message of closeness for an illness or mourning;
4. choose between Egyptian and fuṣḥā simple according to the recipient and the situation;
5. record and understand a voice message in Egyptian.
Nine-week plan (two blocks from 40–45 minutes per week).

The mix. Many Egyptians write a work message in a mix: open in fuṣḥā ( ⁧السلام عليكم ورحمة الله⁩ ), courteous Egyptian body, closure in fuṣḥā ( ⁧مع خالص التحية⁩ ). It's normal and it's not a mistake.
5. Pronunciation

The formulas are also spoken out. Exercise with the section formula 2 until the answer comes out automatically: alf mabrūk! → allāh yibārik fīk · healthy kull w-inta ṭayyib → w-inta ṭayyib. The tone of condolences is low and slow, without emphasis: il-baʾāʾ li-llāh... rabbin yirḥamu.

8. Voice messages

Voice messages in Egypt ( ⁧فويس⁩ · voice) are often more frequent than written ones, even among colleagues. A good voice message: begins with a greeting and the name; state the reason immediately; not more than one minute; closes with a formula (sallim li..., mistanni raddak). Understand a vowel. It is spontaneous spoken: breaks, laughter, noises, changes of theme. The method: 1) listen to everything to understand who, why and what he asks you; 2) listens and records dates, times, places; 3) answer in writing by taking the data (ʿašān atʾakkid: il-ḥadd is-sāʿa Sit down, ṣaḥḥ?).

10. Exercises
Write in Arabic (Egyptian) characters; If you want, add the transliteration.
Exercise 1 · The right formula

What are you writing? a) A friend graduated. · b) A colleague is getting married. · c) Šarīf She had a baby. · d) Yāsmīn She's turning her age. · e) A friend moved to a new house. · f) A friend leaves for Cairo. And what do they say to you, in each case?
Exercise 2 · A full message

Write to Šarīf a message (40–60 words) to invite him to dinner Saturday by you, with: greetings, courtesy request, invitation with day and time, confirmation request, closure. Consistent graphs (section) 3).
Exercise 3 · The register
Write the same content (Tomorrow I cannot come, can we move to Thursday?) to three recipients: a) an Egyptian friend · b) Umm Šarīf · c) an Egyptian teacher you know little (fuṣḥā simple or mixed).
Exercise 4 · Difficult moments

Write a short and suitable message: a) The mother of an Egyptian colleague is in the hospital. · b) The colleague writes to you that he's better. · c) An Egyptian friend's grandfather died. · d) Friend thanks you. What do you say?
Exercise 5 · Answer
What do you say? a) alf mabrūk ʿa š-šuġl il-gdīd! · b) healthy kull w-inta ṭayyib! · c) Ramaḍān karīm! · d) il-baʾāʾ li- llāh. · e) alf salāma ʿalēk! · f) ʿuʾbālak!
Exercise 6 · The holidays

Write your best wishes (one line each, with the appropriate emoji if needed): a) to Umm Šarīf by the end of Ramadan (ʿīd) · b) a Mīna (Coptic Christian) for the Orthodox Christmas of 7 January · c) to the group of Egyptian friends for New Year's Eve
Exercise 7 · Voice message

Record (or write as if spoken) a voice message of 30–40 seconds to Yāsmīn: the memories that Friday there is the party of the course at 7, ask her if she brings dessert, say hello. Then write his written reply confirming the data.

12. Oral and written production
1. Couples (session). The tutor says twenty random formulas (sections 2 and 7); you answer with the answer right away That's right. Then reverse.
2. The phone. Role-playing game: Call an Egyptian friend who has just passed an important exam (or that is sick): greetings, formula, some questions, closure.
3. The chat. With the tutor, a 10-minute written conversation in Egyptian on a message application:
organize an exit, with times, place and a little unexpected. Consistent graphs.

15. Unit verification

Twenty points; Exceeding at least 16. Parts A and B are made in writing (Arabic characters); Part C in voice or in writing. A · Formules (8 points). Write in Egyptian: 1. Happy birthday (to a woman). · 2. A thousand congratulations! · 3. Happy Ramadan. · 4. Heal soon. · 5. I'm sorry for your loss. · 6. God have mercy on her. · 7. Have a good trip. · 8. You're next! B · Responses (6 points). Answer: 9. mabrūk! · 10. Ramaḍān karīm! · 11. il-baʾāʾ li-llāh. · 12. salamtak! · 13. ḥamdilla ʿa s-salāma! · 14. kull sana w-inti ṭayyiba! C · A message (6 points). Write in Egyptian (40–50 words) a message to Umm Šarīf: wish her well for the party, ask for news of the family, tell her that everything is fine in Milan and close with a loving formula. Evaluation of the tutor: formulas (2), appropriate register (2), consistent graphs (2).
